premises.text: Plastic production has led to significant waste and pollution
premises.evidence_span: 7.3 billion tons of plastic have been produced since the 1950s. And 86% of that is waste. 6.3 billion tons of plastic on our land, oceans, air.

premises.text: Plastics are a critical part of the modern economy and a $600 billion industry
premises.evidence_span: Plastics are a critical part of our modern economy. They are an enabling technology in just about every single thing that you and I all love to use. They're a $600 billion industry.

premises.text: Enzymes can be used to break down plastics and return them to the environment
premises.evidence_span: there's another class of polymers called enzymes. And these enzymes can break down those materials and let them go back to the planet where they belong.

premises.text: Current recycling methods are fragmented and inefficient
premises.evidence_span: Recycling is great when it works, but it's fragmented, complex, it's laborious, the margins are low, it's a hard sell.

premises.text: Compostable plastics require industrial composting infrastructure to degrade
premises.evidence_span: you need industrial compost to do that, and those pieces of infrastructure are not all that available.

premises.text: Entropic Materials can stabilize enzymes for use in plastics to enable self-degradation
premises.evidence_span: we're commercializing a breakthrough technology that lets us stabilize enzymes and package them up inside of the plastics so they can self-degrade when we're done with them.

premises.text: The technology can degrade a wide variety of plastics and return them to soil
premises.evidence_span: We can do this with a wide variety of different plastics, and they completely return to the soil at the end of life.

premises.text: The technology can be implemented in simple, scalable infrastructure
premises.evidence_span: that simple infrastructure that's easy to scale and maybe gives us a chance to think about decentralizing our waste stream.

premises.text: The technology can stop microplastics at the source
premises.evidence_span: we stop microplastics at the source.

premises.text: PLA is a significant market for compostable plastics
premises.evidence_span: we're starting with PLA, which is the first compostable plastic. It's a $3.5 billion market.

premises.text: The team has relevant experience and support from reputable organizations
premises.evidence_span: I spent five years at UC Berkeley doing my PhD in materials science and engineering developing this technology, and Jolene has over 11 years of experience scaling up materials in biotech.

value.text: Plastics can be made to self-degrade, reducing environmental impact
value.evidence_span: we're changing the way that we make and break materials so that we can live more harmoniously with nature.
